asset: The arcade nearer its concept: neon ARCADE and PLAY, TICKETS and CLAW, a rocket cabinet, and a fourth gumball machine (Milestone 58)
calls_note: 21 calls in the generation log: 6 edits (4 kept: the cabinet, ARCADE, PLAY with CLAW and TICKETS, and the gumball machine; the first art pass's two edits were redone) and 15 kit isolates (2 kept: one each for the cabinet and the gumball machine; the rest were the first pass's, four drawn from a stale cached painting before the kit fix, and the gumball's first place, moved off the walk).
method: Each edit: a crop of the approved painting (at e10dd213) with a flat-colour block-out of what's added at its exact place; one call repainting the block-out in the room's style; the output registered by searching a uniform scale and offset for the least difference over the crop away from the edit (median difference there reported BEFORE compositing); then only the new thing composited.

edits.name: the rocket cabinet
edits.prompt: This is a crop of an approved hand-painted watercolour game painting of a cozy arcade floor, with one flat-colour block-out added: a small purple arcade cabinet standing on the checkerboard. Repaint ONLY that block-out as a finished, cute arcade cabinet in the painting's soft watercolour and thin warm-brown ink style: a purple cabinet whose front (the face toward the lower left) has a pale lit marquee, a dark screen with tiny pixel stars and a little rocket on it, a sloped control panel with a joystick and round buttons, and a coin door below; on its right side, a glowing neon rocket outline in pink with a teal round window. Keep the cabinet's exact position, outline, size, and perspective, standing on the same tiles. Give it a soft contact shadow on the floor. Change nothing else: every floor tile, every line, the skee-ball lane, and the claw machine stay exactly as they are, pixel for pixel. No text anywhere.
